verdict.rationale: RunAnywhere documents a dedicated VLM API, `RunAnywhere.vlm`, that takes an image together with a text prompt. The Kotlin SDK also states that vision models run on-device, with images staying on the phone, so this is a first-party capability that delivers the core of the story. Missing for 10: a list of supported vision-language models, in-depth VLM docs beyond a one-line description, and independent or hands-on corroboration that image understanding works in practice.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can run vision-language models that understand images alongside text

citations.quote: `RunAnywhere.vlm` takes an image and a prompt.
The RunAnywhere Kotlin SDK runs language, speech, and vision models on the device. Prompts, audio, and images stay on the phone
